slots.staging: Low at ice level, canted dark timber rail disappears into a water opening at right; name and date in upper-left sky. Crew are already ashore. Short reveal, then geography.
View straight down on relief of Antarctic Peninsula at left and Weddell Sea east of it. Label water and land without a wreck pin or exact coordinates. Cut from hull to region.
Reverse at human height, helping hand holds the sleeve of a man scrambling over a ridge. Anonymous period crew partly visible behind. Cold rim light, number high right.

slots.job: Being alive is not being reachable
slots.staging: High oblique above an isolated camp on pack ice. Canvas and bundles cluster far from open water. Type lives over water; no transmitter, land, or artificial SOS.
lettering: NO WAY TO CALL FOR HELP

slots.staging: At the level of a fissure, one isolated pack-ice slab and its fragmenting edges. Frame the stable camp footprint farther back. Small editorial label beside the visible seam.
High diagonal across three clearly separate small hulls pulled onto the same ice, bundles clustered between them. Use open wood and oars as legible silhouettes; no extra craft.
Six simple warm brass counters in an inset of a real wooden tabletop beside a recognizable lifeboat model. Diagrammatic counter set, not a claimed historic artefact. Tight shape composition.

slots.job: Compare boat size and sea crossing
slots.staging: Modern scale comparison with side profile of a small covered wooden boat and a restrained schematic sea-span line on two separate horizontal bands. Boat measure spans its hull; ocean distance has a separate leader. No exact track.

slots.job: The other group cannot know how the voyage ends
slots.staging: Replace visually ambiguous partial counters with a single embossed shelter emblem. Exact 22 WAIT in ivory, centered on slate above the emblem, bottom 25% free.

slots.job: A successful departure still leaves a return problem
slots.staging: Across two pressure ridges toward the low shore-like silhouette of Elephant Island in an editorial schematic, one return direction interrupted by ice. No precise route or implied fourth attempt.

slots.job: Establish the expedition leader before the disaster
slots.staging: Photographic portrait reconstruction in a new seated three-quarter pose, studying a chart at window light, one hand planted to stop chart curling. Name set high beside face; no archive styling.

Straight overhead on a physically rendered contemporary polar relief, conceptual line connects two coasts via the central pole. Use map anchor, neutral land colors and one route. Keep time distinct from actual journey.

slots.job: The ship is the means to the starting coast
slots.staging: Physical model of three-masted Endurance at the sea end of a tabletop relief, land separated by sea. Camera over the water toward coast. Small inset shows intended start area; no exact landing point.
Seen straight down from Endurance's bulwark, floe edges interlock around recognizable timber hull. Two bright masses converge on dark hull. Short date in dark water; no collision spectacle.
Tight over the navigator's shoulder at a period chart table, pencil moving one mark on a generic blank grid, warm cabin key and cold ice outside. Face mostly hidden; no fake original positions.
Low on deck, two crew in profile clear frozen gear and work the same mooring line. White immobile ridges visible past the rail; title small on open ice.

Simple oblique explanatory physical model of a floating plate of ice. Two distinct labeled direction indicators explain forces conceptually; no specific velocities, measured arrows or reconstruction of one date.

slots.job: Show the consequence of the mechanism
slots.staging: Overhead match to previous model. A small recognizable ship is frozen into the same moving plate. Ghost positions belong to the plate outline alone, no free-sailing track. A short precise text sits at lower center above subtitles.
lettering: THE SHIP DRIFTS WITH THE ICE

slots.job: Pressure changes from inconvenience to failure
slots.staging: Macro low at the waterline, ice wedge forces planking inward and a seam bends against normal grain, no explosion or cutaway claim of exact structure. Warm edge of timber against blue.

slots.job: Turn hull failure into an order to evacuate
slots.staging: Interior floor-height view, water spilling over tilted floorboards while boots head uphill toward open light; no face or claimed quoted order. Date and event as editorial text on dark overhead beam area.

slots.job: Show what they could carry away
slots.staging: View from the ice alongside working hands moving a bundled crate past a wooden lifeboat. Distinct empty hold behind at soft focus. Three short labels grouped as single readable stack.

slots.job: Make the actual loss land in silence
slots.staging: From the camp side at eye height, last dark spars tilt into the water beyond a small group seen from behind. Quiet visual payoff to the opening; no oversized silhouette or foreground action.

Return to the planned crossing relief with its interior line faint and the ship position implied offshore without plotted coordinates. Blank interior stands out. Match material of the first polar map.
One cut on the plan. High view of wet ropes and oars laid alongside expedition supplies on ice, suggesting decisions and available means. Editorial line attached visually to the grouped means.
Low with a boot stepping across crusted snow and a taut line stretching toward an off-axis boat; face unnecessary. Arrow of footprints only, no route map.

slots.job: Show why walking was different from hiking
slots.staging: Across the towing line at chest height, men lean away from a loaded hull whose bow is caught on a low ridge. Opposed body angles express tension. Type high over clean white.
lettering: THE BOATS HAD TO COME TOO

slots.staging: Steep overhead, boot track bends around a black crack toward a serrated ridge; hull edge is partial. Use two quiet leader labels pointing to separate hazards.

slots.job: Decision visible in the slack towline
slots.staging: Medium detail of rope dropped slack beside the unloaded boat and a crewman working a tent pole into ice. One decisive state change. Tight crop for physical cause and effect.

slots.job: Put waiting on a directional map
slots.staging: Schematic flat relief of Antarctic coastal region with a broad north arrow offshore. Show an ice plate with tiny camp inset, no pinned coordinates or exact trajectory.
Inside canvas close on several gloved hands dividing a modest ration into small portions with simple period cups. No explicit kills or invented ledger entries. Warm intimate pool of light.
Ground-height close on a dark, widening separation between two slabs, near-side rope fixed to boat, camp gear stays well back. Polar daylight. Type follows open horizontal seam.

slots.job: Commit the three boats to open leads
slots.staging: At the lead's edge, boots on solid ice and hands push a loaded small boat stern-first into a narrow black opening. No man stands where hull will move. Match seam from prior shot.
High diagonal, three boats at distinct distances threading the same lead with oars out, each in open water, no collisions. Compact label points forward toward a dark horizon.
Low angle from land, boots meet dark wet stones while hands hold the nearest boat steady. Label in upper space, rocky ground clearly unlike ice. Crew appears partially, total count is editorial.

slots.job: Put temporary safety on the map
slots.staging: Overhead relief northeast of the Antarctic Peninsula tip. Small named island with a clean leader; expand regional anchor with no invented camp pin. Cool blues switch from documentary closeup.
Contemporary diagram with a compact dark island outside an abstract band of distant marine traffic. Schematic relationship alone; no named lines, exact coordinates or false historical route.
Anonymous back/hand at the camp setting one oar beside other gear and directing attention to the launch point. Camp remains clearly on shore. Shadow and action carry the decision.
Accurate comparative relief showing South Georgia northeast of Elephant Island; both labels must touch land shapes via short leaders. No weather or estimated track plotted yet.

slots.job: Make the length of open water legible
slots.staging: Wider crop of the same geographic family. A single dashed conceptual connection across open sea clearly ends at the two islands. Distances grouped along line; no voyage log claim.

slots.job: Make clear why that island matters
slots.staging: Wide speculative period station silhouettes on South Georgia's inhabited coast, dark roofs and modest jetty at distance, no specific buildings or residents. Label over the settled part of shore.

slots.job: Identify the only boat considered suitable
slots.staging: Three-quarter low side profile on blocks above shingle, oars show scale, two remaining hulls blurred behind. Distinct carpenter viewpoint before changes; name as editorial lettering.

slots.staging: Workshop-like close side angle outside, anonymous carpenter's hands fit an added wooden course along existing gunwale. Physical join clear. One leader points at new plank.
High three-quarter detail of hands tensioning canvas across a partial low covering. Keep working space open. Single material label, no implication of a complete rigid cabin.

slots.job: Explain the original assignment without inventing conversation
slots.staging: On modern planning surface, a labeled name strip is paired visually with the shore group mark. Two zones only, COAST remains pictorial. No faux historical handwriting or meeting scene.
Same tabletop family, new tighter composition of Crean label linked to a stylized boat instead of the shore group. Hand or movement unnecessary; two clear graphic states in separate shots.
Low oblique waterline near Elephant Island, modified James Caird being shoved off with shore crew keeping footing. Broad diagonal from rock to open water. Editorial date over dark hill.
Side-on through sea spray, small covered boat clears surf with partially occluded crew. Camera remains shoreward and behind path of boat. Number printed in compact quiet zone.
Look back from high behind Wild's group toward diminishing boat. Name is editorial, Wild face unidentifiable rear view. The figures stay uphill on rocks, not in surf.
Look from within shadow of shallow ice shelter toward snow streaks outside. Two small figures test opening. Do not depict exact measured natural cavern from excavation photo.
Tight floor detail, moisture falling onto bedding as a hand pulls fabric clear. Shape of icy wall still visible. Text high with two contrasted short lines, no implausible flood.
Three-quarter along an unfinished low wall, two men physically align irregular stones, salvaged cloth and inverted hulls staged separately in middle distance. No mortar or tall hut.

slots.staging: High end-quarter reconstruction so two separate inverted keels and their joint are visible; each rests on wall structure, cloth below and a human crouching at entrance. Fine leaders to hulls and stones.

slots.job: Let low ceiling and human scale speak
slots.staging: Inside view along the underside of two timber hulls, sitting figure cannot stand, amber side-light and canvas. Intimate response to the outer explanatory view.

slots.job: Establish the wait and hand off to sea
slots.staging: From outside, hands secure an edge of the canvas while cold surf glints behind. Place caption away from hands. Tent seam diagonal continues into sail rope on next cut.

slots.job: Communicate tiny island against immense sea

slots.staging: Two faint conceptual directional vectors pass either side of the island while short clear one points to it. No plotted log or degrees. Dark contemporary scientific design, avoid tiny legend.

Shallow side view along working surface: open-frame sextant in gloved hand nearer lens, simple compass farther back, restrained editorial leaders. Use actual sextant construction anchor, no invented instrument readings.
Side framing of a period sextant tilted toward a brief glow through low cloud, sky much larger than boat. Instrument held with realistic grip, no eye line into wrong end.
Close at crew shoulder, horizon diagonal with rolling boat, wet rail and blurred sea behind steadied black metal instrument. No line implies a recorded angle. Text in clean water region.
Four equally clear amber light dots in independent editorial diagram over dark photographic sea texture, no dates or spacing claims. Sober measured tone, avoid fake period page.
Over shoulder to a modern explanatory inset of two joined conceptual vectors over a blank period workspace. Make paper visibly generic, no invented bearings, positions, or log notes.
Near waterline outside wooden hull, hand pours a scoop of water out while other crew retain position, the physical motion points over the side. Upper small title, no water poured inward.
Overhead from stern across three distinct jobs happening in their correct positions, one near tiller, one at sail line, one over rail. One line of typography in upper area, no tags on every person.
Macro of thick white ice on rail with gloved hand knocking it off over water. Big splinters distinct from wood. Type occupies distant dark sea, not the action.
From behind navigator leaning over the near side of vessel, compact position estimate inset without coordinates, bow turned toward a blank horizon. Blue dim dawn.
From boat bow, low cloud opens around distant dark land, slight warm light touches ridge but not a heroic sunset. Eye line forward. Title over cloud, no dock.

slots.job: Put a visible hazard between boat and shore
slots.staging: From landward high side looking down, band of breaking surf separates a small boat from jagged rocks. Clearly keep craft seaward of whitewater. Small label follows surf.
Compression from low boat position toward dark coast, same coast behind broad rising waves, crew checks water gap and keeps distance. Different camera from shoreline observer.
Inside bay looking toward broad dark slope, figures guide boat toward shingle on ropes from a stable shore footing, no cliff surf. Modern geographic anchor for shape only.
South Georgia relief with landing on western side, whaling area farther across the terrain. Short leader labels on opposite sides. No invented village positions or plotted route.

slots.job: Show why the men cannot simply sail again
slots.staging: Intimate aftermath at gunwale, anonymous exhausted man leans his full weight on his arm. Rope slack on shore, boat condition legible without alleging wreck. Let faces and hands carry pause.

slots.job: Show decision to avoid another sea passage
slots.staging: Contemporary geographic abstraction looking along exposed outer coast, restrained line with a clear stop well offshore of rocks. Distinct from prior surf scene and no historical track assertion.
lettering: THE COASTAL ROUTE IS TOO RISKY

slots.staging: Oblique relief following ridges from west to inhabited side. A short directional arrow crossing interior as intent only, not exact glacier itinerary.

slots.job: Place the men remaining by the boat
slots.staging: Mid-distance from higher shingle, three separate figures remain grouped beside secured James Caird. Boat position and posture anchor separation. No invented injuries or tent.

slots.job: Place the three who cross on a new axis
slots.staging: Rear view of exactly three on foot moving uphill away from water. Give each spacing, no boat at summit or modern climbing harness. Date at upper margin.

slots.job: Show terrain that must be read as they go
slots.staging: High oblique across diverging saddles and glaciers, three distant figures encounter route choices on safe foreground ridge. No fictitious arrows if unknown; short factual heading in sky.
Side profile across a steep slope. Two figures brace rope from higher footing, line visibly leads to third lower on the slope. Period rope only, no modern rigging or wrong hand count.
Close oblique along cut steps, short adze blade perpendicular to handle bites a step beneath reaching hand. Same slope angle and rope direction as previous frame, no loose body floating.

slots.job: Communicate steep effort in scale and time
slots.staging: Physically rendered side-section of ice slope with one vertical dimension leader and one duration label separate. Conceptual overview, not exact profile or measured route.
Below crest looking through a narrow pass, three distant figures cross left to right with a wider coastal opening ahead. Single faint light cue, no visible station yet.
Dawn edge crosses boot tracks ending at crest, duration printed quietly against shadow snow. No fake log, no precision timer, no unsupported overnight activity.
Broad high look down toward a small period industrial shore with generic shed silhouettes and jetty. Three figures approach in foreground. No modern manager's villa or precise architecture.
Three anonymous figures on western shore gesture toward safe help at a distance. Avoid showing a particular transfer method or invented identifiable rescue craft. Compact text above far slope.
Map family again, tiny South Georgia and Elephant Island with blank sea between. Design compares the two places without a crossed invented signal path.

slots.job: Return to the group in a single image
slots.staging: View from just inside fabric opening toward grey empty water with two men attending an ordinary task. Group total as text, no need to show twenty-two bodies.
From ceiling height in low shelter, hands mend cloth and move supplies in their respective places. Period materials, warm inside and harsh light at door. Small orderly label.
One person checks dark horizon through opening as another continues simple shelter work. Opposite focus from previous interior. Text sits in sky, no imagined wreck.
lettering: NO WORD FROM THE JAMES CAIRD

slots.staging: Close at bedding height, two hands roll a worn sleeping bag firmly. Keep identity off camera; daylight at the low entrance makes routine visible.

slots.job: Show effect of routine on group
slots.staging: Medium oblique toward doorway, two crew tighten a bundle or tend shelter supplies. Name omitted; use an editorial intention label without invented quotation.

slots.job: Show elapsed time without invented dates
slots.staging: Low exterior of weathered canvas under new frost at first light. Familiar shelter silhouette, changed accumulation, exact same roof arrangement. Time heading small.
Editorial shadow of an unidentifiable ship behind a solid wall of ice in a labeled schematic, no detailed vessel rendering, no false position. One tracked line stops short.
Warm ivory column on dark slate with full vessel name and an open blank distance to the small island shape. Give the longer name two clean lines; no made-up log or exact sailing route.
Third entry on same editorial system, interrupted line fades well before shore and a small unidentifiable schooner silhouette cues class. Distinct shape with same visual grammar.
Wide structured composition with three completed stop marks aligned outside the ice boundary, single island still separated. Three exact marks, no fourth to spoil later payoff.

slots.job: Make time create a survival cost
slots.staging: From chest height under roof, hands turn an almost empty period supply bag over a plain metal plate. Other people off camera. Enough warm light to see scarcity.
Ground level along shore, fingers reach at low tide toward visible limpets and seaweed on wet rocks, hands distinct from crash zone. Two compact leaders label the items.

slots.job: Introduce the new source of help
slots.staging: Modern editorial closeup of the southern coast of Chile on tactile relief and an inset simple ship bell silhouette. No invented official paperwork, port mark or state crest.
Three-quarter at dock height, low dark tug, single capped funnel and both masts recognisable from archive. No visible face for Pardo without verified reference; command is in the typography.
Low side-on angle of small steel tug alongside loose ice at safe spacing, a visibly light bow profile. Text concise, no fake scale lines or exact hull claims.
A physical schematic with uninterrupted white pack barrier across frame and small silhouette outside, its path visibly ends. No collision.
At water level behind tug leaving view, single funnel and two masts in credible order. No invented harbor landmark. Steam and wake draw eye toward departure.
Local schematic map north-up with Elephant Island silhouette, patterned pack to northeast, one clearly distinct northwest approach arrow. No exact route; words and directions agree.
Shoulder-level bridge angle anonymous uniformed officer from behind with hand on period steering control, looking through opening to water. Funnel and masts respect viewpoint, no radar.
Low outside tug looking through fog, fixed icebergs flank narrow visible water gap. Correct relative scales, no ship embedded in ice or abstract glacier wall.
Reverse high above open water behind the near tug, far shore barely resolves through fog. Small label at clearing, no clear crowd yet.

slots.job: Establish arrival without spoiling shore reaction
slots.staging: Atmospheric long view from seaward past tug silhouette toward same rocky headland. Put date in a restrained zone over fog. No men ashore facing ship yet.

slots.job: Set up the confusion while the men prepare food
slots.staging: Close by cold daylight at entrance, hand pauses above a vessel and one man starts to look up. Offscreen call; no ship in shot and no invented speaker identity.
Documentary editorial two-line comparison above an anonymous man looking from meal vessel toward sound, letterforms distinct but same scale. Exactly the two attested phrases.

slots.job: Reveal rescue through the men's eyes
slots.staging: Reverse from rocky shoreline, two men from behind turn toward the offshore tug, separated by a band of water. Resolve on the same sightline. No large vessel at beach.

slots.job: Make the relief worth the wait
slots.staging: Tight profile of one anonymous survivor gripping a companion's shoulder, gray surf soft behind. Specific human reaction with no invented words. Count shown above eye line.

slots.job: Explain relation of shore to tug
slots.staging: Wide three-plane reconstruction using rescue composition anchor, rocky shore foreground, small open transfer boat in middle distance, recognizable tug safely offshore. No exact count or tow device asserted.
Tighter side of dark tug with hands reaching across deck railing while anonymous men steady each other. Do not show all twenty-two at once; count editorial.
On deck from shoulder level, sailors relax their grips and look back at sea. Faces visibly tired. Short text over open sky with ample still hold.
Clean polar relief shifts from Weddell side to opposite Ross sector, geography visible throughout. No presenter; map performs clarification directly.

Match the BAS polar orientation. The Ross Sea is in the deep lower bight below the ice shelf near the 180° meridian, geographically separated from the peninsula. Draw a leader from exact ROSS SEA PARTY above right to that point in open water.

slots.job: Give losses clear and sober weight
slots.staging: Modern editorial memorial typography over quiet Ross Sea ice relief, three modest marks with no named portraits or invented deaths. No sunset triumph.
Return to plan as a fine incomplete line over Antarctic relief, no fictitious traversal. Different crop emphasizing uncompleted interior; subdued color.
Two restrained editorial clusters and clear sum layout using names of group roles. No crowd photo or icon count required; no mixing in Ross Sea group.
Tight modern typography of total with small restrained silhouette of recognizable three-masted ship. Typography clear and exact; visual echo of first ship shot.

Quiet unoccupied opening in pack ice from a higher point of view, absence of hull carries the loss, simple total statement in open sky. Soft clear dawn and restrained camera, no triumphal scene or unsupported reunion.
